With ordinary split availability such as 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, every morning slot is rejected by the afternoon interval and every afternoon slot by the morning interval, leaving no available slots even for a personal event.       "body": "This find searches for an override that excludes the slot and rejects the slot as soon as one is found. If a date has overrides for 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00, a valid 10:00 slot is rejected because it precedes the second override, while a valid 14:00 slot is rejected because it follows the first. Multiple windows on one date therefore produce no availability. The check should accept a slot covered by any override window."
    },

      "line": 117,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",

      "body": "The override checks reject only wholly disjoint slots, so any partial overlap is accepted. For a fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override, a 10:30–11:30 round-robin slot supplied by another host passes these checks and reaches the dateOverrideExist return true, despite the fixed host being unavailable for its final half hour. A slot beginning exactly at 11:00 is also accepted. Validate both the slot start and slot end against the override boundaries."
    },

      "line": 110,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Identify overridden days using the organizer's calendar date",
      "body": "Override existence is determined from the date of its UTC-shifted start, rather than the organizer's overridden calendar day. For example, a fixed host in Asia/Kolkata with a Tuesday 00:30–01:30 override has an interval starting Monday at 19:00 UTC. A Tuesday 10:00 IST slot from another host consequently does not match the override's date and falls back to the fixed host's regular working hours, potentially exposing the rest of Tuesday as available. Determine the overridden day in the host's timezone before checking the converted interval."

      "severity": "high",

      "body": "The end variable is calculated from slotStartTime again, so this check never verifies that the event finishes before the host's closing time. For example, with a fixed host working 09:00–17:00 and another host's date override generating a 16:30–17:30 slot, both start and end are evaluated as 16:30 and the fixed host is marked available. Use slotEndTime and require the complete event to fit within a working-hours interval."
    },

      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Split converted overrides at the invitee's midnight",
      "body": "Adding the timezone offset and then retaining only hour and minute loses calendar-day rollover. A UTC override from 17:00–19:00 viewed in UTC+6 becomes startTime 1380 and endTime 60. buildSlots discards this as an invalid start >= end range, so the valid 23:00–01:00 availability disappears. The next day cannot recover it because activeOverrides only selects by the override's start. Convert full timestamps and split or clip the interval against each invitee day."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/lib/slots.ts",
      "line": 214,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Avoid applying the DST adjustment twice to overrides",
      "body": "These offsets are calculated on the override's date, so the converted minutes already account for that date's DST. buildSlots subsequently applies organizerDSTDiff minus inviteeDSTDiff again, as it does for recurring working hours normalized using current offsets. If today is in winter, a July 10:00–11:00 override in America/New_York viewed in UTC is converted correctly to 14:00–15:00 here, then shifted to 13:00–14:00 by buildSlots. The router can then reject that shifted slot entirely. Overrides need to bypass this additional recurring-hours DST correction."
    }

findings.title: Continue checking busy times after matching a date override
findings.body: When an override exists for the slot's date, this branch returns true before checking busy. For example, an override allowing 10:00–11:00 makes that slot available even when an existing booking or calendar event occupies 10:00–11:00. This affects both fixed and round-robin hosts. An override should replace normal working hours, not bypass calendar and booking conflicts.

findings.title: Require a matching working-hours interval instead of rejecting on any nonmatch
findings.body: The working-hours check rejects a slot when any interval for its weekday excludes it. With ordinary split availability such as 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, every morning slot is rejected by the afternoon interval and every afternoon slot by the morning interval, leaving no available slots even for a personal event. Availability must require at least one matching interval, rather than require compatibility with every interval.

findings.title: Treat multiple date-override windows as alternatives
findings.body: This find searches for an override that excludes the slot and rejects the slot as soon as one is found. If a date has overrides for 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00, a valid 10:00 slot is rejected because it precedes the second override, while a valid 14:00 slot is rejected because it follows the first. Multiple windows on one date therefore produce no availability. The check should accept a slot covered by any override window.

findings.title: Require the complete event to fit inside the override
findings.body: The override checks reject only wholly disjoint slots, so any partial overlap is accepted. For a fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override, a 10:30–11:30 round-robin slot supplied by another host passes these checks and reaches the dateOverrideExist return true, despite the fixed host being unavailable for its final half hour. A slot beginning exactly at 11:00 is also accepted. Validate both the slot start and slot end against the override boundaries.

findings.title: Identify overridden days using the organizer's calendar date
findings.body: Override existence is determined from the date of its UTC-shifted start, rather than the organizer's overridden calendar day. For example, a fixed host in Asia/Kolkata with a Tuesday 00:30–01:30 override has an interval starting Monday at 19:00 UTC. A Tuesday 10:00 IST slot from another host consequently does not match the override's date and falls back to the fixed host's regular working hours, potentially exposing the rest of Tuesday as available. Determine the overridden day in the host's timezone before checking the converted interval.

findings.title: Use the event's end time when checking working hours
findings.body: The end variable is calculated from slotStartTime again, so this check never verifies that the event finishes before the host's closing time. For example, with a fixed host working 09:00–17:00 and another host's date override generating a 16:30–17:30 slot, both start and end are evaluated as 16:30 and the fixed host is marked available. Use slotEndTime and require the complete event to fit within a working-hours interval.

findings.title: Split converted overrides at the invitee's midnight
findings.body: Adding the timezone offset and then retaining only hour and minute loses calendar-day rollover. A UTC override from 17:00–19:00 viewed in UTC+6 becomes startTime 1380 and endTime 60. buildSlots discards this as an invalid start >= end range, so the valid 23:00–01:00 availability disappears. The next day cannot recover it because activeOverrides only selects by the override's start. Convert full timestamps and split or clip the interval against each invitee day.

findings.title: Avoid applying the DST adjustment twice to overrides
findings.body: These offsets are calculated on the override's date, so the converted minutes already account for that date's DST. buildSlots subsequently applies organizerDSTDiff minus inviteeDSTDiff again, as it does for recurring working hours normalized using current offsets. If today is in winter, a July 10:00–11:00 override in America/New_York viewed in UTC is converted correctly to 14:00–15:00 here, then shifted to 13:00–14:00 by buildSlots. The router can then reject that shifted slot entirely. Overrides need to bypass this additional recurring-hours DST correction.
